articles.title: Call my (estate) agent! Why celebrities are always buying each other’s homes
articles.summary: If you’re seeking a discreet mansion with secluded grounds and plenty of room for your own memorabilia, you may want to remember Joe Pesci’s mistakes before trying the open market. Last year, Austin Butler bought a mansion from Brad Pitt.
body: If this makes it sound to you as if there are only a handful of celebrity-friendly homes on earth, and celebrities spend their lives swapping them around among themselves, then you’re right.

According to Mohamed Mussa, the managing director of Chestertons Global, this is partly by design. In an op-ed that has been doing the rounds, Mussa explains that celebrities often require things in properties that civilians like us might not consider, such as gated entrances, secluded grounds, space for staff and layouts designed to keep fans at bay.

“In 2020, Los Angeles City Council passed an ordinance allowing tour buses to be banned from residential streets judged unsafe,” he explains, which has to be useful. I once had a fairly major freakout after buying my house because I didn’t check the details properly and missed that the plumbing under my kitchen sink consisted of an Evian bottle sellotaped to a pipe. Imagine how much worse it would be to buy a house and realise that a packed bus parks outside your front door three times a day so that tourists can try and take a picture of you putting the washing out.
points: If you’re seeking a discreet mansion with secluded grounds and plenty of room for your own memorabilia, you may want to remember Joe Pesci’s mistakes before trying the open market.

articles.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping review – surreally awful prequel to the Katniss Everdeen era
articles.summary: Overwrought and boring, this nadir of a prequel to the Games’ death match saga is nothing but a cash grab for an exhausted franchise. Here is yet another iteration of the utterly exhausted, unbearably extended and now surreally boring Hunger Games franchise, based on the YA bestsellers by Suzanne…
body: Well, “reaping” in fact refers to an annual process by which ordinary smudgy faced, raggedy clothed people are chosen at random for compulsory participation in this futurist dystopia’s brutal, televised survival contest to the death: a bread-and-circuses nightmare with which the rulers keep the populace in a cowed and pacified state. In this Darwinian process, competitors strategically team up with (and then betray) some players against others in the short term, to stay in the game.

As ever, the “televisual” aspect of this is represented in the retro-style TV screens, but no one is ever shown actually watching these Games; Haymitch and his proletarian, quasi-hillbilly community don’t have TVs, but where is the middle class who are supposedly glued to their sets? Jesse Plemons is marginally less caricatured and tiresomely ridiculous as the organiser Plutarch Heavensbee, the younger version of the role earlier played by the late Philip Seymour Hoffman. But, really, this film has no actual interest and no authentic reason to exist, other than to gouge an income stream out of its fanbase.

articles.title: ‘Sorry, I’m still in love with Daniel Craig’: Ralph Fiennes, Brad Pitt and more react to Robert Pattinson as James Bond
articles.summary: Former 007 George Lazenby was supportive while The Lighthouse director Robert Eggers reveals what Pattinson was doing when the news broke • Robert Pattinson is James Bond. What happens next? • Peter Bradshaw’s take • Pattinson’s journey to James Bond • Behind Bond’s bankability.
body: Film industry figures including Ralph Fiennes, Brad Pitt and former Bond actor George Lazenby have reacted to the news that Robert Pattinson has been cast as the new 007.

Pitt was asked about Pattinson while promoting his new film, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, and responded: “I think it’s a great choice. I love what that guy’s been doing. He’s been making such interesting choices, and then for him to balance it out, it’s really cool.” Pitt then made a playful pitch for a villain role in Bond 26, winking at the camera and saying: “Get Denis Villeneuve on the flip phone. Let’s go.”

Fiennes, meanwhile, was being interviewed with his castmates from The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping (in which he plays President Snow) on Sirius XM, and initially appeared somewhat downbeat, saying: “I’m sorry. I’m in love with Daniel Craig still. It’s hard. I’ve got the wrench in my heart.” But Fiennes, who played Gareth Mallory (who became secret service chief M) opposite Craig in Skyfall, Spectre and No Time to Die, added: “[Pattinson] is a great actor. I’m sure he’ll be great.”

articles.title: Climate Change Visibility Rises in Mainstream TV and Film, USC Norman Lear Center Study Shows
articles.summary: Stories about the causes and effects of climate change are on the rise in mainstream TV and film, according to a study released Tuesday by USC Norman Lear Center in partnership with Good Energy.
body: The report tracks how often climate change appears in scripted entertainment, as well as what that looks like on screen. It comes on the heels of the release of eco-comedy “Digger,” which stars Tom Cruise as an eccentric oil magnate who accidentally causes an ecological disaster. The film was a bomb at the box office, by Cruise’s high standard, but the storyline’s focus on climate change got a lot of attention in the promotional campaign leading up to the Warner Bros. film’s U.S. release on Oct. 2.
This new research updates and expands on the 2022 report, “A Glaring Absence,” which analyzed 37,453 scripts from 2016-20 and found 36 climate-related keywords appeared in only 2.8% of them.

This year’s report tracks the original 36 keywords, plus an expanded list of 105, across 35,120 scripts from 2021 to 2024. It also tracks quantitative narrative analysis across 100 climate storylines and qualitative analysis across 30 climate storylines. In general, most of the discussion centers around the destructive impact of climate change rather than causes or efforts to find systemic solutions.
points: Stories about the causes and effects of climate change are on the rise in mainstream TV and film, according to a study released Tuesday by USC Norman Lear Center in partnership with Good Energy.

articles.title: ‘Madden’ Review: Nicolas Cage Plays John Madden as the Disheveled Buddha of Football in David O. Russell’s Eccentric Stunt of a Sports Biopic
articles.summary: "Madden" is a stunt biopic on cinematic amphetamines. At times, the film can feel like an extended "Saturday Night Live" sketch played straight. But it’s like an "SNL" sketch shot and edited by Scorsese.
body: Cage dons a jowly fatsuit to play the Oakland Raiders coach-turned-sports commentator. It's two parts impersonation, one part Nicolas Cage kabuki.

You could say that every movie writes its own rules. But you can really say that about a movie in which Nicolas Cage, buried under a jowly fatsuit that makes him look like Jiminy Glick playing John Candy, portrays John Madden, the celebrated coach of the Oakland Raiders in their mean-machine ’70s heyday, who went on to become one of the most unhinged — and influential — TV sports commentators of his era.

“Madden” features one more stylized semi-prosthetic character: the Oakland Raiders’ owner, Al Davis, played by Christian Bale with a shark mouth and slick receding hair and a Jewish goombah accent and a princess-doll wife (an unrecognizable Sienna Miller), all of which makes you think he must be some sort of vicious criminal. But no, Davis is just Madden’s fellow monomaniac (the relentless businessman to Madden’s football artist), and these two sustain a testy friendship even once Madden leaves the team.
points: "Madden" is a stunt biopic on cinematic amphetamines.
At times, the film can feel like an extended "Saturday Night Live" sketch played straight.
But it’s like an "SNL" sketch shot and edited by Scorsese.
It's two parts impersonation, one part Nicolas Cage kabuki.

articles.title: Amelia Dimoldenberg on Ending ‘Chicken Shop Date,’ the Biggest Celeb Flirts and What’s Next: ‘I’m Taking Time to Write’
articles.summary: Amelia Dimoldenberg is breaking up with “Chicken Shop Date.” After 12 years, the beloved interview series — in which Dimoldenberg awkwardly attempts to flirt with some of the biggest celebrities in the world, from Andrew Garfield to Cher — is coming to an end next week.
body: When she started the show, Dimoldenberg was a “17-year-old who had never gone on a date before … I know, it’s shocking,” she told the audience at the world premiere of the “Chicken Shop Date” movie Monday night in London. “Now, I’m going through a massive break-up, so pray for me.”

In a Q&A with presenter Lea Ogunlami before the movie — which contains interviews with Role Model, Jorja Smith, Noel Gallagher, Nemzzz, Jack O’Connell and a secret final guest — Dimoldenberg reminisced on her favorite memories from the chicken shop.

“I know an episode’s going to be huge if they flirt with me,” she said when asked if there’s a formula to which dates go viral. “If they flirt with me back, it’s going to be a win. But a lot of the time they don’t, which is kind of annoying.”
Asked to name the flirtiest celebs, Dimoldenberg revealed: “Damson Idris, I think that’s my mom’s favorite one. Andrew Garfield, obviously. Billie Eilish. Daniel Kaluuya.”

articles.title: ‘Mick Jagger should fold up his penis and go home’: the caustic genius of music critic Robert Christgau
articles.summary: Beloved for his savage takedowns and rhapsodic raves, the legendary Village Voice reviewer opens up in a candid new documentary. Rows and rows of CDs, albums, cassettes and books creak and groan on shelves that snake around the walls and choke the halls of an apartment in New York City’s East…
body: Welcome to the lair of Robert Christgau, the self-declared “Dean of American Rock Critics”, as seen in a new documentary provocatively titled The Last Critic. “Bob is someone who has probably listened to more music, and published more words about music, than anyone to walk the face of the earth, and he’s still doing it in his mid-80s,” says Matty Wishnow, who directed the film. “It’s a career that’s both unprecedented and unrepeatable.”

Wishnow says he was inspired to make the documentary by the formative influence Christgau had on his taste growing up. “I would open his collections of Consumer Guides and wonder: ‘Why is Queen a C- and Billy Joel a B- while this group called The Roches is an A+?’ It scrambled my brain and made me think of the idea of commercial versus credible and popular versus sub-popular,” he says. “When people ask me why I’m not into Yes or James Taylor, I think 30% of my answer is personal and 70% is something Bob wrote that imprinted itself on me.”

articles.title: Brad Pitt and Florence Pugh pitch for James Bond villain role
articles.summary: The two A-list stars throw their hats into the ring to be the villain facing Robert Pattinson's 007.
body: We have barely come up for breath since Robert Pattinson was picked as the new James Bond, but A-listers are already jostling for position to play his enemy in the next 007 movie.
A the premiere of his new film in Hollywood on Monday, Brad Pitt was asked by Extra TV, external if he would like to play the villain in director Denis Villeneuve's forthcoming spy movie.
With a wink at the camera, the star replied: "Robert! Denis! You know, I'd like to do that. I'd be up for that. My man Javier [Bardem] did it so well. It's tall shoes, but I'd take that on."

Bardem played Bond baddie Raoul Silva in 2012's Skyfall, opposite Daniel Craig. Asked the same question by Complex, external later, Pitt was still enthusiastic: "Sign me up for the villain. Get Denis Villeneuve on the flip phone, let's go!"

articles.title: Woman who accuses Russell Brand of rape says prison message 'upsetting'
articles.summary: Mia Latter spoke to the BBC after the jailed comedian claimed he was innocent of offences against four other women, in comments on a podcast following his convction.
body: A woman who has made allegations against Russell Brand has said she finds it "upsetting" and "really shocking" that he was able to claim he was innocent from prison, following his conviction for rape and sexual assault.

Speaking after the comedian's wife Laura read out a message from him on their Sunday Service show on YouTube, Mia Latter told BBC Radio 4's Today programme she found it "appalling" to hear "this Christian message alongside absolute lies".
"I just felt for those women that stood trial and everything they went through," she said.
Latter, 37, who has alleged she was raped by Brand when she was 16, was not a complainant in his recent criminal trial and he denies her claims.

articles.title: Billy Evans Fires Back at Amanda Seyfried and Nathan Fielder: “It’s My Life and I Love It”
articles.summary: In his first print interview about 'You Can See Everything,' Elizabeth Holmes’ partner pushes back on his portrayal as a controlling opportunist, responds to the 'Dropout' actress' efforts to break them up — and reveals what Holmes thinks of his nude scene: "A violation of our intimacy."
body: The whole point of participating in Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim ’s You Can See Everything, says Billy Evans, was to change the world’s perception of Elizabeth Holmes, the 42-year-old founder of Theranos currently serving out an 11-year sentence for defrauding investors.
Evans, 34, is an MIT grad whose latest business venture — a company similar in ambition to Theranos called Haemanthus — is also raising eyebrows.

He broke his silence first with a Nov. 2 “Ask Me Anything” on X, where he addressed speculation about cocaine use (he said his drugs of choice are coffee and nicotine and that his persistent screen sniffles were the result of cedar allergies). He also denied being gay (“In 2026, being gay is considerably more socially acceptable than being in love with Elizabeth Holmes,” he wrote).

But Evans has a lot more to say. In his first print interview about the film, he wants to respond to Amanda Seyfried, 40, who recently told Rolling Stone that making the film, “I became this weird Billy Evans detective because I had gotten such strong negative feelings from him in the footage.” After filming their contentious dinner together, her opinion of him “only got worse.”
